title: Man. Post. Cap. VI: PLAC proves conceded; GAR 2 in quo / PLAC deny immediate
pass_a_gloss: I then asked for the scriptural place. An act of God's mind is knowable only by revelation. He runs instead to Augustine and Martyr, who were not, I think, given that divine act by name from heaven. I already allow a kind of oneness in Adam by species and origin; I refuse the leap that God therefore treated them as one so as to impute Adam's first actual sin immediately. I also refuse numeric oneness / one individual man. Thus he establishes what I grant and never meets what I deny. GAR 2: if 'in whom all sinned' marks imputation of Adam's sin (as earlier claimed), and imputation is God's declaring all guilty for Adam's sin, then those words, if they mean all were regarded in Adam as one man, also mean God so regarded them. PLAC: the Apostle never said all sinned in Adam; and even if he had, the words would not mark Adam's-sin imputation—at least not immediate—as we showed earlier and will confirm later.
pass_b_english: Next I asked whence he had it—that is, from what divine Scripture. For such an act of the divine mind cannot be known from elsewhere than from God's revelation. But he flees to Augustine and Martyr, to whom such a divine act was not, I think, revealed from heaven by name. Then I did not deny that all men were somehow one in Adam—namely by unity of species and of origin; I only denied that it follows from that that they were so considered by God as one that He immediately imputed to them Adam's first actual sin. I also denied that they were considered as one numerically, or as an individual man. Therefore he proves what I concede; what I deny he does not even touch. GAR. 2. Since the Apostolic words 'in whom all sinned' denote the imputation of Adam's sin, as was confirmed above, and that imputation is an act of God declaring all guilty on account of Adam's sin, it follows that if those words signify that all were considered in Adam as one man, they designate by the same reason that they were so considered by God. PLAC. Neither did the Apostle say that all sinned in Adam; nor, if he had said it, would those words denote the imputation of Adam's sin, at least not immediate, as we both showed above and will confirm below.
source_text: Deinde quaesivi, unde haberet, hoc est, ex qua divina Scriptura. Talis enim actus mentis divinae aliunde quam ex Dei revelatione cognosci nequit. Ille vero confugit ad Augustinum, & Martyrem, quibus talis divinus actus non est, opinor, nominatim caelitus revelatus. Tum non negavi omnes homines aliquomodo unum fuisse in Adamo, nempe unitate speciei, & originis, tantum negavi inde sequi fuisse ita a Deo tanquam unum consideratos, ut illis primum Adami peccatum actuale immediate imputaverit. Negavi etiam fuisse consideratos tanquam unum numero, seu individuum hominem. Itaque ille probat quod concedo, quod nego ne attingit quidem. GAR. 2. Cum Apostolica verba, in quo omnes peccaverunt, imputationem Adamici peccati denotent, ut est supra confirmatum: imputatio autem illa sit actus Dei declarantis omnes ob Adami peccatum reos, consequens est, ut, si ea verba significant omnes in Adamo consideratos ut unum hominem, designent eadem ratione, a Deo ita fuisse consideratos. PLAC. Nec Apostolus dixit omnes in Adamo peccavisse; Nec si id dixisset, verba illa denotarent imputationem Adami peccati, saltem immediatam, uti & supra ostendimus, & infra confirmabimus.

lemmas.gloss: by unity of species and of origin

choices.choice: Concede species/origin unity; deny in quo yields immediate imputation
